We need to propose a retrosynthesis route (max 3 steps) to target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We need leaves commercially available, total price <= $9999. Need to produce JSON route with reaction nodes (template_id) and molecule nodes.

We need to find suitable retrosynthetic disconnections: The molecule has a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide (C= C - C(=O)N- aniline). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl-phenyl-CH=CH-CO-N-phenyl-NH2? Actually the amide is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) meaning the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline that also has an NH2 (para? Actually Nc3ccccc3N is an aniline with an amino at para? The SMILES: Nc3ccccc3N indicates an aniline with two amino groups? Actually "Nc3ccccc3N" is an aniline where the nitrogen is attached to the aromatic carbon (as substituent) and also the ring has an NH at the other position (maybe para). So it's a diamino phenyl.

Thus target can be assembled via sulfonylation of p-tolyl amine with sulfonyl chloride derived from the other phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Then the other phenyl sulfonyl chloride can be made from sulfonylation of phenyl with SO2Cl2? Actually typical route: start from p-toluidine (commercial) and sulfonyl chloride of 4-(trans-α,β-unsaturated amide) phenyl sulfonyl chloride. Or reverse: first make the sulfonyl chloride from the second phenyl, then couple with p-toluidine.

Alternatively, we could form the amide via coupling of trans-cinnamic acid derivative with aniline.

Simplify: Disconnection 1: Break the sulfonamide N-S bond: target -> p-toluidine (commercial) + aryl sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonyl fluoride) of the other phenyl.

Disconnection 2: The aryl sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the phenyl ring bearing the unsaturated amide. That phenyl can be made via Suzuki coupling? But maybe we can start from 4-bromo-phenyl sulfonyl chloride? Actually we need the phenyl sulfonyl chloride with the unsaturated amide substituent. Could be made by sulfonylation of the phenyl with SO2Cl2 then attach the unsaturated amide via Friedel-Crafts? Not straightforward.

Alternative route: Build the molecule via sequential sulfonylation and amide formation.

Step 1: Form the amide: start from trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) to give trans-cinnamoyl anilide (C= C - C(=O)N-Ph-NH2). This is the fragment: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N attached to phenyl sulfonyl group.

So we can have fragment A: trans-cinnamoyl aniline (with an extra NH2). This can be made by coupling trans-cinnamic acid (or its acid chloride) with p-phenylenediamine (commercial). Use amide formation (acid chloride route). So step: trans-cinnamic acid + SOCl2 -> cinnamoyl chloride (commercial? maybe not). But we can use standard amide coupling reagents (EDC) but for retrosynthesis we can consider the amide bond formation as a step.

Thus we can disconnect the amide bond: target -> (aryl sulfonyl chloride) + p-toluidine? Wait the amide is attached to the phenyl sulfonyl group via the phenyl ring (the phenyl bearing the unsaturated amide). So the amide is attached to that phenyl as a substituent (para?). Actually the SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has the unsaturated amide substituent at para position relative to the sulfonyl connection? The sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl via S(=O)(=O) attached to N of p-tolyl sulfonamide. So the phenyl sulfonyl group is attached to the N of p-tolyl sulfonamide. The phenyl sulfonyl group also has the unsaturated amide substituent.

Thus we can disconnect the sulfonamide N-S bond: gives p-toluidine (commercial) and sulfonyl chloride of the phenyl with unsaturated amide substituent (call it 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride). That sulfonyl chloride can be made from the corresponding sulfonic acid (or from the phenyl sulfonyl chloride) via chlorination.

Alternatively, we could disconnect the C=C bond (retro-aldol) but not needed.

Goal: 3 steps max. So propose:

Step 1 (final): Sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride -> target.

Step 2: Synthesize 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride from 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonic acid (or from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride via Suzuki coupling with trans-cinnamyl boronic acid). Simpler: start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and perform Suzuki coupling with trans-cinnamyl boronic acid (commercial) to install the unsaturated amide? Wait trans-cinnamyl boronic acid is C6H5-CH=CH-B(OH)2, not the amide. Actually we need a trans-cinnamoyl amide attached to phenyl, not just cinnamyl. So we could start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride, then do Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylonitrile? Not.

Alternative: Build the unsaturated amide on the phenyl after sulfonyl chloride formation: Step 2: sulfonyl chloride formation from 4-bromo benzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) then Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylonitrile? Not.

Maybe better: Step 2: Form the amide first on a phenyl ring, then sulfonyl chloride formation. So we start from 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) and trans-cinnamic acid to make 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)aniline (the amide). Then sulfonyl chloride formation on that aniline? But we need sulfonyl chloride attached to the phenyl via S(=O)2Cl, not via N. So we need to sulfonylate the aniline nitrogen later with p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl group attaches to the N of p-tolyl, not to the phenyl. So the phenyl bearing the amide is attached to the sulfonyl group via the sulfonyl nitrogen (i.e., the sulfonamide N is attached to p-tolyl, and the sulfonyl S is attached to the phenyl ring). So the phenyl ring is attached to S, not N. So we need a sulfonyl chloride attached to that phenyl (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we can start from 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)aniline (the phenyl with amide and an NH2). Then convert the aniline to sulfonyl chloride? Not possible; we need sulfonyl chloride on the phenyl ring, not on the amine.

Thus we need aryl sulfonyl chloride with the amide substituent already present on the ring. So we need a phenyl sulfonyl chloride that is para-substituted with the unsaturated amide. This can be made by sulfonylation of the phenyl ring (i.e., sulfonyl chloride is attached to the ring via S=O2Cl). Starting material could be 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonic acid (commercial?) maybe not. Could be made by sulfonation of 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzene (i.e., p-cinnamoylbenzene) using chlorosulfonic acid to give sulfonyl chloride. So step 2: sulfonation of p-cinnamyl phenyl (i.e., trans-cinnamyl phenyl) to give sulfonyl chloride.

Thus route:

Step 1 (final): Sulfonamide formation between p-toluidine and 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride.

Step 2: Synthesize 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride from trans-cinnamic acid + 4-bromobenzene? Actually we need the phenyl ring with a trans-cinnamoyl substituent at para position relative to sulfonyl group. So we can start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and perform Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylonitrile? Not.

Better: Start from 4-bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and do Suzuki coupling with (E)-3-(4-aminophenyl)acrylonitrile? The coupling would attach a phenyl group, not the unsaturated amide.

We need to attach a trans-cinnamoyl amide substituent onto the phenyl ring. That could be done via amide formation after Suzuki coupling of a phenyl boronic acid with a bromobenzenesulfonyl chloride to give a biphenyl sulfonyl chloride, then amide formation on the second phenyl? Not.

Alternative: Build the unsaturated amide on the phenyl after sulfonyl chloride formation via Friedel-Crafts acylation with cinnamoyl chloride? But Friedel-Crafts acylation on sulfonyl chloride may be problematic.

Given limited time, maybe propose a simpler route using commercially available building blocks: Use p-toluidine, 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (commercial) and then attach the unsaturated amide via amide coupling on the sulfonyl chloride? Not.

Maybe we can propose a 2-step route: Step 1: Couple p-toluidine with 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride (made in step 2). Step 2: Make 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride from 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride? Not.

Given constraints, we can assume availability of 4-(trans-cinnamoyl)benzenesulfonyl chloride as a commercial chemical (maybe). Let's check via search catalog.
